title: Testing REST APIs with Postman
idea: Postman lets you save API requests in a collection, attach tests to their responses, and replay the whole set after every change.
points: A collection is an ordered set of requests; the Collection Runner sends them all.
`{{base_url}}` is a variable: Postman fills it in before it sends the request.
Tests live in the post-response script; results show in the Test Results tab.
A script can save a value, such as a new `id`, for later requests.

walk.text: The `books` table, seeded as before. The server under test is the Express app below.
`POST` stores a book and answers 201 with the stored row.
`GET` answers with the book, or 404 when no row matches.
`DELETE` answers 204, or 404 when it deleted nothing.
Listen on port 0, then close the server and the pool so the script exits.
`check` prints PASS or FAIL. `send` wraps one `fetch` call and returns status and JSON.
Four requests in order. The new `id` stands in for `book_id`; each `check` mirrors a Postman test.

pitfalls: Requests that reuse `book_id` fail if the `POST` that sets it has not run.
A collection that creates data should delete it afterwards, or reruns see leftovers.
Without tests, a run only shows responses; add `pm.test` checks so failures are visible.

options: PASS GET gives 200, FAIL GET gives 404, 1 failed
FAIL GET gives 200, PASS GET gives 404, 1 failed
FAIL GET gives 200, PASS GET gives 404, all passed
quiz.why: The status is 404, so the first check fails and the second passes. `failed` counts one failure. `fetch` does not throw on a 404.

takeaway: Save requests, add tests, and replay the collection after every change.
